slides.heading: Start with a repeatable session
slides.body: Choose an easy setup and record it.
slides.narration: Start your TRX workout with supported squats, rows and presses, then progress the setup. This short IZEM guide is for generally healthy adults learning suspension training. Choose an easy angle and start with one controlled set. If you have an injury, a medical condition or trouble with balance, get advice on suitable exercise first. Stop a movement that hurts.

slides.heading: Check your equipment first
slides.body: Follow your trainer and anchor instructions.
slides.narration: Inspect the straps for wear and use the anchoring system supplied for your trainer. Follow the installation and testing instructions before every session. Keep the floor clear and dry. If you cannot confirm that the setup is secure, leave the straps unloaded and ask the manufacturer or a qualified trainer for help.

slides.heading: Learn the movements
slides.body: Squat, row, press and supported split squat.
slides.narration: The written guide gives an example starting session with supported squats, low rows, chest presses and supported split squats. Both feet stay on the floor for the split squat. A floor glute bridge and modified floor plank round out the example without teaching foot-cradle exercises at the same time. Read the movement instructions and linked demonstrations before trying an unfamiliar exercise. The sample amounts are starting examples, not a prescription for everyone.

slides.heading: Adjust one thing at a time
slides.body: Body angle changes rows and presses.
slides.narration: For a row, moving your feet a little toward the anchor generally lets you lean farther back. For a standing chest press, moving your feet back toward the anchor lets you lean farther forward. Reverse that adjustment to make either exercise easier. These cues apply to those two movements. They are not a universal rule for every suspension exercise. Keep your range of motion consistent and return to an easier setup if you lose position.

slides.heading: Compare the same setup
slides.body: More repetitions alone can be misleading.
slides.narration: Imagine you do ten rows on Monday. On Thursday you stand farther from the anchor, stay more upright and manage fourteen. The easier angle changes the comparison. Record the anchor, strap setting and starting foot position along with repetitions and effort. Ten repetitions becoming twelve with the same setup is a more comparable result. These numbers are hypothetical examples, not promised outcomes. Do not turn your body angle into an invented kilogram load.

slides.heading: Leave time to recover
slides.body: Two separate days are a practical starting schedule.
slides.narration: Two sessions on separate days, such as Monday and Thursday, are a practical starting schedule. Build up gradually if you are inactive and allow more recovery when needed. If you already lift weights, count this work as part of your training. Rest between exercises long enough to regain control of your breathing and technique. You do not need to race through the list.

slides.heading: Read the routine and copy the log
slides.body: Use the linked guide for details and sources.
slides.narration: The complete article includes exercise instructions, manufacturer safety links and a copyable setup log. IZEM supports workout planning around your equipment and schedule, plus set logging. Check that the movements you need are supported before relying on an app for this routine. Ask a qualified trainer to check unfamiliar movements and your anchor setup in person. Read the guide at youraicoach dot life slash blog slash TRX workout.
